To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the core promoter region of several cancerous gene promoters contains nucleotide hexameric signals that are conserved across the species.
the nucleotide hexameric composition in the promoters of several cancerous driver genes are different from the non-cancerous driver genes.
the nucleotide composition of a promoter sequence plays a significant role in gene activation and that the promoter sequence is the most important region in a gene for gene expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of signals present in the promoter regions.
the study of signals in the promoter regions and their classification and their role in cancer.
the identification of the signals in the promoter sequences of several cancerous and non-cancerous driver genes and the classification and clustering of these signals based on the base composition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nucleotide hexameric sequences present in the core promoter regions of the driver genes of the melanoma pathway have been identified and classified.
the core promoters of several cancerous and non-cancerous human genes contain nucleotide hexamer sequences, with a few nucleotide differences between them, that are likely to be recognized by TFs.
the signals are indeed present in the promoters of the melanoma carcinoma pathway and other non-cancerous pathway genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the promoter region of the driver genes of the melanoma pathway have the major classes of the signals in the promoter regions.
the promoter regions of cancerous genes have the same signals that are present in the non-cancerous promoter regions.
the hexamers are not only present on the promoters of cancerous genes but also on non-cancerous ones and that they are present on miRNAs as well.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are some hexamers which are more frequent in the cancerous genes and some which are more frequent on the non-cancerous ones.
the signals in the core promoter are present in the promoter regions, and that these signals are conserved across the species and are also present in the melanoma carcinoma pathway.
the hexameric nucleotide composition of the promoter regions of cancerous genes is not random.
